summary: The required reparse-deferral coverage gap was introduced by g0016. Before the change, the skip behavior did not exist; afterward, the old harness cannot reach it.

claims.necessity_reason: The review established that the target must exercise the default-enabled deferral skip for a partial token.

before.requirement: Exercise the same reparse-deferral skip on a later nonfinal parse call.
before.reason: The verified preimage has no callProcessor definition, and both old parse routes invoke the processor directly. The skip behavior was not present.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The old direct XML_Parse route calls the processor without a deferral helper.
The old buffered route also calls the processor directly.

after.requirement: Exercise the default-enabled skip by making a later nonfinal parse call on the same parser while a partial token has insufficient new data.
after.reason: The new helper contains the skip. Each fresh target parser gets only one nonfinal call, when the saved byte count is zero, followed by a final call that bypasses deferral.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Initialization enables deferral and sets the saved partial-token count to zero.
The direct XML_Parse route calls the new helper.
The buffered route sets finalBuffer before calling the helper.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: The recipe identifies the fixed xml_parse_fuzzer_UTF-8 target.

claims.comparison_reason: The after-side unsatisfied condition is the new deferral guard. Before the change, neither parse route had that guard, so the same coverage obligation was not applicable.
